approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs using only accepted scores from the current session. A greedy population of sixty-four scored molecules supplies rank-selected parents; connected-fragment crossover and short sequences of atom, bond and ring edits build a fresh field of 160 candidates for each announced batch of ten. Stable molecular identity, duplicate rejection and the inherited sulfur admission rule determine which products enter that field. A Gaussian process trained on every accepted observation uses radius-two chiral Morgan environment counts in 2048 bins and generalized Tanimoto similarity. Correlated posterior draws select the paid batch. After three consecutive batches without an incumbent improvement, selection is restricted to the forty highest predictive means until the next improvement. Count features therefore influence both the predictive mean, including this eligibility ranking, and the residual covariance that supplies sampled exploration. The Parent has already removed a dormant mutation-effort floor; the separately sampled mutation continuation remains active.
approach.novelty: Remove occurrence multiplicity from that shared feature representation by replacing each cached count with its presence indicator. The same vocabulary and kernel formula remain, so the intervention removes how many times an environment occurs while retaining whether it occurs. The new evidence is this component's total contribution on the current stall-masked Parent. Earlier count removals used an earlier Parent without that mask; current siblings changed allocation consumers, mutation continuation, or the complete search method. This single removal tests whether multiplicity remains useful when it also controls the restricted eligible set. It predicts changed paid molecules and a lower final mean if the retained information still contributes. It does not separate predictive-location and residual-covariance effects.

observed_bottleneck: The ticket addresses an unresolved dependency of the current Parent's paid decisions: count multiplicity is active throughout its predictor, but its conditional contribution has not been measured after the stall eligibility mask was added. The actual n-cf8d309c06de summaries and run.log files for all three Search seeds are complete, with macro mean 0.607030316211131 and population SD 0.030175277546149237; seed macros are 0.649701282562401, 0.585233817344553 and 0.586155848726439. Reading its fifteen session logs finds multiplicity in all 435 fitted training matrices, maximum logged count 40, 435 full pools and 88 restricted batches, with no posterior fallback. Its 4,350 paid records have full/late sequential incumbent-increment mass 5.978073077532332/1.0224077547621127, so late paid progress remains limited, but this does not establish a count-feature defect. Dedicated derivations are policy/scratch/r0061-02-improve-L01/audit-seed-0-zaleplon_mpo.json and the corresponding audit-seed-<Search seed>-<task>.json files, each citing its actual summary, run.log, session log and trajectory. Historical complete controls n-b9f2c3328d4c, n-161b32768a03 and n-b77e5493be1e lost 0.038794771343121, 0.08822718632415433 and 0.03715967951388403 respectively against their own earlier sulfur-gated Parent. Their full analysis records distinguish total removal, location-only removal and residual-covariance-only removal; they support a conservative removal-loss prediction but cannot settle this masked-host question or be summed into a decomposition. The current catalog explicitly marks their conditions mismatched to n-cf8d309c06de.
hypothesis: Remove m-000000000003 occurrence multiplicity at the shared FingerprintPosterior.features cache boundary on code Parent n-cf8d309c06de. At every existing cache miss compute the identical inherited radius-two, chiral, 2048-bin count vector c, then store (c > 0).astype(c.dtype) as the active cached row. Every training, pool/query and previous-emission probe reads that same binary row. Retain kernel(x,y)=dot(x,y)/(sum(x*x)+sum(y*y)-dot(x,y)), including its existing empty-vector convention; on binary rows this is exactly binary Tanimoto. Consequently both predictive location and full residual geometry can change, and the same stall predicate can select a different top-forty mean-ranked set. The causal path is multiplicity removal -> changed active similarities and posterior distribution -> naturally changed paid identities -> changed accepted training/breeding history -> potentially lower complete endpoints if the removed information remains useful. Only the total feature-information removal is identified; no consumer-specific mediation or interaction is claimed.

finding_summary.headline: Multiplicity removal changed every batch and lowered the mean by 0.05415
finding_summary.insights:
The result resolves the current stall-masked Parent’s missing total multiplicity comparison. Presence alone preserved the feature vocabulary but lost useful information under this composition. On the Child’s own paid molecules, the passive count reference predicted observed scores more accurately: MSE 0.009801 versus 0.018240, unequal-label pair ordering 0.739 versus 0.640, and mean within-batch Spearman 0.591 versus 0.367. These are associations on the selected stream; they cannot identify how much of the endpoint loss came from predictive means, residual covariance, eligibility, or later path divergence, and they do not label the reference’s unpurchased choices. The complete paired result supports the retained component at the registered descriptive scale; it establishes neither statistical significance nor transfer to a new ordinal model.

The method still spends most late proposals on local refinement: only 192 of 2,175 late molecules beat their original best generating parent, compared with 238 for the Parent. The Molecular assessment shows a larger inventory of typed/generic scaffolds (2,161/1,499 versus 1,667/951) alongside a jump in oversized proposals from 22 to 374 and repeated assemblies of inherited heteroaromatic motifs. Fragment-excluded nearest-prior similarity remains high (0.8815 versus 0.8863), so the extra scaffold strings do not demonstrate broad architectural exploration. Some oversized molecules do improve incumbents, and compact leaders also occur; a universal size penalty is not established. The combined evidence points to limits in recognizing repeated motifs and proposing distinct, chemically coherent core arrangements. A representation that preserves multiplicity addresses the observed ranking deficit, while a topology-aware proposal operator that changes cores without repeatedly concatenating the same motifs could address the remaining search behavior; its score benefit is untested. Reactive local bonds and unspecified stereochemistry limit chemical plausibility independently of the measured benchmark score. This node settles the registered total removal on this host and leaves consumer-specific attribution, alternate representations and proposal methods open.
finding_summary.results: Multiplicity disappeared exactly from all training, pool and next-fit probe features under positive repeated-count exposure. Kernels and posterior predictions changed in all 435 batches, and every batch selected a different paid set from its same-state count reference. Of 4,350 paid molecules, 2,211 were absent from that reference set; all 2,136 with a subsequent-fit opportunity entered the next fit and probe, and 876 later served as breeding parents. All fifteen task/seed runs completed without a posterior fallback. The final mean fell from 0.607030 to 0.552880, a paired change of -0.054150. All three seed averages fell (-0.105274, -0.021738 and -0.035439), while individual endpoints comprised eleven losses and four gains. The mean losses were largest for sitagliptin_mpo (-0.149132) and deco_hop (-0.103777); the former triggers the protocol’s paired task-regression rule. The registered removal-loss prediction is supported, so this is a confirmed removal mechanism and positive conditional evidence for retaining occurrence multiplicity on this Parent. It is a score loss, with neither a technical failure nor a refuted removal-loss prediction.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich carbonyl heterocycles and arylamines, with a large repetitive-molecule tail and unresolved reactive bonds and stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All five objectives and Search seeds 0/1/2 are covered: 300 accepted observations per session, including 10 supplied initial records and 290 optimizer proposals. Both Child evaluation and pairing with the published code Parent n-cf8d309c06de are complete according to the frozen context.comparison; no trajectory path or matched session is missing. Only these Search observations were read. The 4350 Child and 4350 Parent optimizer structures parse in the recorded RDKit environment; parsing is not evidence of stability, synthesis or biological utility. Child ring-closure text rates are 0.9793 to 0.9920 and aromatic-text rates 0.9644 to 0.9862. The output is rich in fused/bridged rings, aryl groups, carbonyl-containing N heterocycles and halogenated arylamines. Functional-group variety and graph scaffold variety are present, but many proposals remain close analogues or repeated assemblies of the same motifs. Drug-likeness is judged weak because substantial oversized assemblies and reactive local groups coexist with otherwise ordinary medicinal-chemistry fragments. The full/late paid denominators are 4350/2175, with late defined as optimizer ordinals 146 through 290. Child versus Parent fragment counts at <=6 heavy atoms are 57 versus 98 full and 31 versus 36 late; oversized counts at >=60 are 374 versus 22 full and 245 versus 0 late. Full heavy-atom min/p10/median/p90/max are 1/23/29/55/120 versus 1/24/28/34/96; late they are 1/24/29/68/120 versus 1/24/28/34/57. Distinct nonempty typed/generic Murcko scaffolds are 2161/1499 versus 1667/951 full and 1063/738 versus 774/414 late; empty-scaffold molecules are 66 versus 95 full and 34 versus 36 late. Session-summed first appearances after initial coverage are 2210/1587 versus 1736/1054 full and 938/630 versus 693/339 late; these are session events, not pooled unique counts. Mean nearest-preceding-accepted raw-count generalized Tanimoto is 0.872228 versus 0.869800 over 4350 queries each. Excluding <=6-heavy-atom queries and references gives 0.881509 over 4293 versus 0.886317 over 4252; no eligible query lacks a preceding eligible reference. Late means are 0.884906 versus 0.883926 over 2175 each, and 0.894729 over 2144 versus 0.895855 over 2139 after exclusion. Thus the small all-row increase does not survive removal of the fragment tail. Neither scaffold count nor this similarity is a quality score. No fragment improves its session incumbent. Of the 374 oversized Child proposals, 19 improve the incumbent, with summed increments 0.016996850896114437; 18 of those events occur on the same objective. These selected-stream associations are not independent support for an endpoint or attribution to the representation change. Across the Child stream, 643 proposals contain N-halogen bonds, 309 O-halogen bonds, 137 peroxides and 591 saturated carbons with at least two nitrogen neighbours, versus 888/162/118/687 for the Parent. These are structural alerts, not measured toxicity or instability. Twenty-four proposals in each stream have a carbon bonded to multiple halogens, so the historical assertion that such a group is impossible is not supported by these trajectories. No Child proposal specifies an atomic stereocentre or carries formal charge; RDKit perceives 5084 unassigned stereocentres in total. Neutral encoding does not prove the absence of protonatable amines. Reproducible evidence is in policy/scratch/r0061-02-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-audit.json and audit-{child,parent}-seed-{0,1,2}-{task}.json in that directory: all heavy-atom counts, full/late per-session values, signed Child-minus-Parent differences, chronological scaffold first appearances, actual-score associations and every input hash. The source manifest preserves the original trusted staging identity and SHA-256 of each Child trajectory; run-contained copies are explicitly derived byte-identical evidence, not published Child trajectories. Parent inputs are the published nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/seed-{0,1,2}/trajectories/{task}.jsonl files. The exact authority is policy/requests/r0061-02-improve-L01-molecular-assess-6ca69692195b0766.json. The unchanged raw-count diagnostic formula was checked in nodes/n-cf8d309c06de/optimize.py. Audit versions: Python 3.10.20, NumPy 1.26.4, RDKit 2023.09.6. Chemistry differences are descriptive associations on this panel, not mechanism activation, component attribution or a future experiment selection.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals are mostly compact carbonyl-linked aromatic heterocycles: heavy-atom median 25, p10/p90 23/28, range 1 to 51; median four rings and two aromatic rings. Ring/aromatic text rates are both 0.9851. The initial indole carboxanilide has methoxy groups and a fluorophenyl amide. Later leaders retain aryl/carbonyl character but add aza bridges, N-O substitution or N-N-containing fused rings. The seed-0 leader is a 24-heavy-atom, five-ring carbonyl compound; the seed-1 leader has 24 heavy atoms and six perceived rings. Such dense connectivity is chemically more demanding than an ordinary substituted indole. The stream contains 166 N-halogen, 171 N-N-single-bond and 15 peroxide-bearing proposals. Parent median size is also 25, but its median ring count is three; Child nonempty typed/generic scaffold counts are 462/230 versus 186/69. More graph frameworks therefore coexist with essentially the same size window. Audit: policy/scratch/r0061-02-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-audit.json#per_task/zaleplon_mpo.
liabilities: N-fluoro/N-chloro groups, N-N linkages and peroxides complicate chemical stability assumptions; 217 proposals contain a perceived three- or four-membered ring.
Dense fused/bridged connectivity and unspecified stereochemistry make synthetic plausibility questionable without geometry or route evidence.
missing_features: Consistent retention of the compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement during structural exploration is missing: both fragments and coupled larger structures lose score. The observations do not identify an unseen target-specific functional group.
Stereochemically defined, less crowded alternatives to the bridged leaders are not demonstrated as a reliable high-scoring series; no score benefit of configuration assignment is established.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Child leaders score 0.4349635367667153 at seed 0/evaluation 100 and 0.43495883620084 at seed 1/evaluation 243. The higher observed decile has heavy-atom median 25, versus 32 in the lower decile; zero-score SBr and a 46-heavy-atom coupled structure scoring 4.779918081864987e-22 show that both severe truncation and growth can lose the rewarded pattern. The visible association favours compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangements rather than atom accumulation. Seed 2 ends with an N-fluoroamide/hydrazine-containing molecule scoring 0.2933971259571244, below its earlier best 0.4163503402962837. Parent bests for seeds 0/1/2 are 0.42348216717712805, 0.4387992465191 and 0.45050436981567554; the Child differs in topology without uniformly improving this local chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: This is the dominant growth tail. Among 870 proposals, 343 have >=60 heavy atoms versus 10 for the Parent; 240 of 435 late proposals remain in that tail versus none for the Parent. Child heavy-atom min/p10/median/p90/max are 1/31/49/103/120 versus 1/26/32/39/96. Median ring and aromatic-ring counts are both six, versus four for the Parent. The seed-1 leader is a 102-heavy-atom, 16-ring assembly repeating carbonylated N/O heteroaromatics, aryl ether links, chloromethyl groups and small fused carbocycles, with a terminal nitrile-containing aryl system. Seed 0 builds large linked carbonyl-rich N heterocycles; seed 2 instead favours a smaller linked pair of carbonyl-rich fused heterocycles bearing N-F/N-Cl. All are neutral and stereochemically unspecified. Nonempty typed/generic scaffold counts rise to 506/427 from 346/240, but fragment-excluded nearest-prior count similarity rises to 0.919756 from 0.889824, consistent with large repeated local environments. Audit: policy/scratch/r0061-02-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-audit.json#per_task/deco_hop.
liabilities: Large multi-unit aromatic assemblies carry substantial size and synthetic-complexity liabilities; the tail reaches 120 heavy atoms and 21 perceived rings.
Peroxides occur in 81 proposals, N-halogen bonds in 270, and chloromethyl/alpha-chloro ether motifs occur in leading assemblies. Their scores do not establish handling stability or feasibility.
missing_features: Efficient coverage of compact heteroaromatic/decorated alternatives is missing from the strongest Child series; the paired Parent demonstrates higher scores without repeated multi-unit expansion.

Stable linking chemistry accompanying the repeated motifs is not reliably present. These trajectories do not reveal a unique missing target motif or prove that simply shrinking a molecule improves it.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Small ClCl and F proposals score 0.5, while the initial carbonyl-rich heteroaromatic ester scores 0.548381482770623. Child bests across seeds 0/1/2 are 0.5992204110559887, 0.6102565643213362 and 0.6013013118916631, at 68, 102 and 35 heavy atoms respectively. The higher decile has heavy-atom median 95 versus 31 in the lower decile; 40 of its 87 molecules contain a peroxide. Repeated decorated heteroaromatics therefore accompany modest local score increases in these Child paths, but are not shown to be necessary: Parent bests are 0.8561477222467935, 0.6217289889933668 and 0.6442339647723496 at only 30, 36 and 28 heavy atoms. Oversized Child proposals supply 18 incumbent improvements with total increment 0.01408118994892471; they are not all fruitless, but most observed progress occurs elsewhere. The final seed-2 structure scores 0.5957269700332963. The evidence cannot specify which unobserved decoration would recover the missing score.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring chemistry comprises halogenated aryl groups connected to aliphatic amines: flexible branched diamines in seeds 0/1 and compact bridged diamines in seed 2. The 870 proposals have heavy-atom median 30, p10/p90 24/42 and range 2 to 80; median three rings and one aromatic ring. Halogen text rate is 0.9885. The seed-2 leader has 27 heavy atoms, six perceived rings, a bromophenyl group and an aryl O-F bond. Seed-0 and seed-1 leaders have 26 and 28 heavy atoms and only one and two rings respectively. Amine functionality is already present, so absence of basic centres is not the bottleneck these molecules show. There are 427 proposals with saturated carbon bonded to at least two nitrogens and 99 with O-halogen bonds. Parent median size is 29, with median four rings and two aromatic rings; Child/Parent nonempty typed/generic scaffold counts are 339/247 versus 326/201. Audit: policy/scratch/r0061-02-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-audit.json#per_task/drd2_docking.
liabilities: Aryl O-F connectivity in the highest-scoring structure is a chemical reactivity concern; it should not be conflated with ordinary carbon-bound fluorination.
Aminal-like carbons, crowded fused rings and unspecified configurations weaken synthesis/stability confidence even when an accepted score is high.
missing_features: The missing chemical capability is reliable access to comparably scored amine/aryl structures with routine stable local bonds and less demanding cage topology, rather than a basic nitrogen that is already present.

Assigned configurations for stereogenic amine-bearing ring systems are absent. Formal-charge encoding is also absent, although these neutral amines may be protonatable; no score benefit of either change can be inferred here.

per_task.generated_character: The stream consists largely of N-methylated cyclic carbonyl compounds and lactam/urea-like rings fused or bridged to phenyl/aza-aryl groups, often with ethoxy, propyl or amino substituents. The open-chain/conjugated 25-heavy-atom example scores 0.047432239931849314, a smaller aryl amide 0.07504633196017493, and N scores zero. per_task.generated_character: The proposals retain carbonylated fused N heterocycles from the initial chemistry and decorate them with aryl fluorine, fluoromethyl/fluoroalkenyl substituents, primary amino groups and sometimes N-fluorination. The 870 proposals have heavy-atom median 27, p10/p90 23/35 and range 1 to 60; median four rings and three aromatic rings. The seed-1 leader is a 27-heavy-atom, four-ring dicarbonyl heterocycle attached to an amino-substituted benzocyclobutane-like system with fluoromethyl groups and an N-F bond. Seed 0 reaches a cumulated-double-bond ring system; seed 2 retains a fused heteroaromatic carbonyl framework with amino and fluoroalkenyl groups. Cumulated-double-bond text rate is 0.2437; N-halogen bonds occur in 179 proposals, O-halogen bonds in 72. Parent median size is 26 with p90 29 and median four rings/two aromatic rings. Child/Parent nonempty typed/generic scaffolds are 296/194 versus 274/101. Audit: policy/scratch/r0061-02-improve-L01/molecular/chemistry-audit.json#per_task/sitagliptin_mpo.
liabilities: N-F and O-halogen bonds, small fused rings and cumulated-double-bond ring systems raise stability and geometry questions; accepted graph validity is not a synthetic route.
Oversized coupled heterocycles can have vanishing observed scores, while smaller late variants can also score poorly, so a size-only rule would miss important connectivity differences.
missing_features: Reliable construction of compact amino/carbonyl/fluorinated arrangements with chemically routine local bonds is incomplete; the score-visible gap is not simply insufficient fluorine or insufficient ring content.

Stereochemical specification of the amino-bearing small-ring leaders is absent. The trajectories do not identify an exact unseen pharmacophore or show that stereochemistry accounts for the Parent difference.

Child bests for seeds 0/1/2 score 0.4816443933649283, 0.5750823714049933 and 0.5262308379606722 at 27, 27 and 25 heavy atoms. All 87 higher-decile structures contain carbonyl and halogen groups, with heavy-atom median 27; the lower-decile median is 48. The 60-heavy-atom coupled heterocycle scores 1.6758614448245604e-53 and a 56-heavy-atom example 5.4391203474237023e-42. transferable_gaps.evidence: Source n-b5a14afe9b35 versus published code Parent n-cf8d309c06de, Search seeds 0/1/2 only, five sessions per seed, 290 accepted optimizer proposals per session; full/late chemistry-audit.json under policy/scratch/r0061-02-improve-L01/molecular records 57/31 fragments <=6 heavy atoms versus 98/36, and 374/245 oversized molecules >=60 versus 22/0. No fragment improves an incumbent. Nineteen oversized Child proposals do improve incumbents, so the upper tail is not uniformly unproductive. The largest expansion repeats carbonyl-rich heteroaromatic units; compact high-scoring molecules also occur. These are observed-stream associations under this exact comparison, not a component contribution.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generated size distribution is not consistently controlled while retaining useful scaffold connectivity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs ways to vary or repair a scaffold without collapsing it to a tiny fragment or repeatedly concatenating its existing motifs. Any size handling should preserve the observed exceptions and remain a chemistry capability, not an assumed universal size reward or a task-specific threshold.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On n-b5a14afe9b35, the same complete Search panel contains 643 N-halogen, 309 O-halogen and 137 peroxide-bearing optimizer proposals, versus 888, 162 and 118 in n-cf8d309c06de; chemistry-audit.json records exact structural predicates and per-session denominators. High observed scores coexist with aryl O-F, N-F and peroxide-containing assemblies. Twenty-four molecules in each stream already have multiply halogenated carbon, so inability to form that class is not supported. Bond alerts are chemistry readings, not measured stability or toxicity.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ordinary halogenated scaffolds are not reliably distinguished from reactive heteroatom-halogen and peroxide connectivity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic chemical vocabulary should distinguish carbon-bound halogen substitution from formation of N-halogen, O-halogen and O-O bonds and support stable alternatives around the same core. Local bond context, rather than elemental presence alone, is the missing distinction; no particular objective or utility gain is implied.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All 4350 optimizer proposals of n-b5a14afe9b35 have zero specified atomic stereocentres and zero formal-charge-bearing molecules, consistent with the digest counters. The same structures contain 5084 RDKit-perceived unassigned stereocentres in chemistry-audit.json; the Parent stream also lacks specified stereochemistry. The evidence is the accepted Search output only, not proof that the implementation cannot represent such states or that the scores distinguish them.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted structures leave stereogenic geometry undefined even when they build complex saturated ring systems.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator lacks demonstrated output coverage of specified configurations and explicit ionisation alternatives. A task-agnostic representation could preserve or explore these states where chemically meaningful, while recognising that neutral amines may already be protonatable and that this panel establishes no score advantage from changing state encoding.

transferable_gaps.evidence: For n-b5a14afe9b35 in the complete Search panel, 1124 proposals contain a perceived three- or four-membered ring and 591 contain a saturated carbon with at least two nitrogen neighbours; Parent counts are 1172 and 687. Twenty-six Child proposals have an all-aromatic perceived ring of size <=4, versus 170 for the Parent. Leading Child structures include 24 heavy atoms with six perceived rings and bridged amine frameworks. chemistry-audit.json records the predicates; these counts do not mean every small ring or aminal is infeasible.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring novelty is often expressed as crowded fusions or bridges without accompanying evidence of feasible geometry or synthesis.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs topology-aware construction and access to routine ring/linker alternatives, with local assessment of strained fusions, bridges and stereochemistry. Graph sanitisation or increasing the number of scaffold strings alone does not establish that a proposed topology is makeable.

The repeated-assembly stream increases that similarity while adding scaffolds. Full/late, signed session differences and all first-appearance events are preserved in chemistry-audit.json. These metrics neither rank chemical quality nor explain the endpoint causally.
transferable_gaps.gap: Larger scaffold inventories do not consistently translate into exploration beyond repeated local chemical motifs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic exploration should make alternative core arrangements and linker chemistry available without relying on repetition of an existing motif to produce a new scaffold identifier. Distinguish meaningful architectural changes from graph-string novelty; diversity itself remains descriptive rather than a guaranteed reward.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
